paper.title: Algorithm 642: O(n) computation of a cubic smoothing spline fitted to n noisy data
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 12(2), June 1986, pp. 150-153 (the archive header says ACM TRANS. MATH. SOFTWARE, VOL. 12, NO. 2, JUN. 1986, P. 150)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 642.gz (scouted 2026-11-27, gz sha256 fea2d2ad84a7883c2a45f04844cfb56b6112992cda5e485d6c47e01c0ae58f19). One Fortran file: CUBGCV and subroutines SPINT1, SPFIT1, SPCOF1, SPERR1, GGRAND, the test driver CUBGCV TEST DRIVER, and the shipped printed output 'CUBGCV TEST DRIVER RESULTS:' with the 'FOR CHECKING PURPOSES' block.

claim.seed: DSEED = 1.2345D4 in the test driver (GGRAND is a multiplicative congruential generator, 7^5 mod (2^31-1), so the input data are fully determined by this seed)
claim.location: Shipped printed output of the CUBGCV test driver, inside 642.gz (the text after the driver's END statement, headed 'CUBGCV TEST DRIVER RESULTS:'): the summary VAR, GCV and mean square residual, and the fitted values Y and standard errors SE at points I = 1, 21 and 41 from the 'FOR CHECKING PURPOSES' block. The driver fits a cubic smoothing spline with JOB=1 to 50 points y = sin(3 pi x / 2) plus uniform noise in [-0.3, 0.3].

reference.file: CUBGCV TEST DRIVER RESULTS block in 642.gz (the driver source and its printed output are in the same file)

claim.metric: Nine printed values from the driver output: VAR, GENERALIZED CROSS VALIDATION, MEAN SQUARE RESIDUAL, and Y and SE at I = 1, 21 and 41 (the reference's 'FOR CHECKING PURPOSES' values).
claim.paper_value: Not located in the paper text (paywalled); the shipped printed output is the only value to check.

values.name: TEST driver CUBGCV VAR (error variance estimate)
TEST driver CUBGCV GENERALIZED CROSS VALIDATION
TEST driver CUBGCV MEAN SQUARE RESIDUAL

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference prints 4 decimal places (F8.4, F7.4), so its rounding unit is 1e-4 and the half-unit is 5e-5. A tolerance of 1e-4 allows one unit in the last printed place, and no more. The driver's seeded generator is deterministic, so the printed values should reproduce exactly on a correct build; the tolerance covers only the print rounding. Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: one fit of 50 points.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; a CACM/ACM TOMS Collected Algorithm. The rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped driver generates its own noisy data from a fixed seed and calls CUBGCV to compute a smoothing spline with GCV and error variance; the printed fit values depend on the O(n) factorisation and the GCV minimisation, which the paper describes but which cannot be read off the paper alone.
